title: Spatial Pattern Matrix
description: Raven's style visual matrix puzzles & spatial reasoning.

questions.questionText: Analyze the circle pattern addition matrix. In each row, the third circle is the union of the first two. Which circle completes the grid?
questions.explanation: The rule is addition: Column 3 = Column 1 + Column 2. In Row 3, we add (Top-Left + Bottom-Right) and (Top-Right + Bottom-Left), which gives a circle with all four quadrants colored.

questions.questionText: Observe the rotation of the triangles in the matrix. Each triangle rotates 90 degrees clockwise from left to right. Which direction should the missing triangle point?
questions.explanation: Each triangle rotates 90 degrees clockwise in each step: Up -> Right -> Down. Row 3 follows Down -> Left -> Up. Thus, the missing triangle points Up.

questions.questionText: In this grid of houses, each row and column contains a unique combination of roof shapes (Triangular, Flat, Curved) and door shapes (Rectangular, Arched, Square). Which house completes the pattern?
options: House with Flat roof and Rectangular door
House with Curved roof and Arched door
House with Triangular roof and Square door
House with Flat roof and Square door
questions.explanation: Following the Latin Square rules, each shape combination must occur exactly once in each row and column. The missing cell must contain a Flat roof (the only roof shape missing from Column 3 and Row 3) and a Rectangular door (missing from Row 3 and Column 3).

questions.questionText: Observe the progression of star points. The number of points increases incrementally in each row. Which star completes the grid?
questions.explanation: Points increase cell-by-cell. Row 1 has stars with 3, 4, 5 points. Row 2 has 4, 5, 6 points. Row 3 has 5, 6, 7 points. Therefore, the missing star has 7 points.

questions.questionText: Identify the relationship between the outer container shape and the inner shape in the grid. What completes the final row?
questions.explanation: The outer container shape is constant per row (Row 1: Circle, Row 2: Square, Row 3: Triangle). The inner shape progresses (Square -> Triangle -> Circle) shifted by one. For the last cell in Row 3, the container is a Triangle, and the inner shape is a Triangle.

questions.questionText: Observe the orientation and count of internal lines within each square cell. Which square completes the bottom row?
questions.explanation: Row 1 contains vertical lines (1, 2, 3). Row 2 contains horizontal lines (1, 2, 3). Row 3 contains diagonal lines (1, 2, 3). The missing square must have 3 diagonal lines.

questions.questionText: Count the number of dots inside each triangle cell across the grid. What is the correct dot count for the missing cell?
questions.explanation: Dots count increases across and down: Row 1 has 1, 2, 3 dots. Row 2 has 2, 3, 4 dots. Row 3 has 3, 4, 5 dots. The final cell must have 5 dots.

questions.questionText: Look at the color distributions of the houses in each row and column. Which house color completes the matrix?
questions.explanation: Each row and column must contain exactly one Red house, one Blue house, and one Yellow house. Row 3 contains Yellow and Red, so the missing house must be Blue.

questions.questionText: An 8-slice circle has a single shaded slice rotating clockwise. Observe the pattern to guess the missing state.
questions.explanation: The shaded slice starts at index 0 (Slice 1) and moves 1 slice clockwise in each step: 0 -> 1 -> 2. In Row 2 it is 2 -> 3 -> 4. In Row 3 it is 4 -> 5 -> 6 (Slice 7). Therefore, index 6 (Slice 7) is shaded.

questions.questionText: Each cell contains concentric circular rings. Discover the growth rule to identify the correct missing ring count.
questions.explanation: Concentric rings count increases: Row 1 has 1, 2, 3 rings. Row 2 has 2, 3, 4 rings. Row 3 has 3, 4, 5 rings. The missing circle contains 5 concentric rings.

questions.questionText: What is the next number in the sequence: 3, 5, 9, 17, ?
questions.explanation: The difference between consecutive numbers doubles each time: +2, +4, +8, +16. 17 + 16 = 33.

questions.questionText: Find the missing square number: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ?
questions.explanation: The sequence consists of square numbers: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², and the next is 6² = 36.

questions.questionText: Complete the numeric progression: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The difference increases by 2 each time: +4, +6, +8, +10, +12. 30 + 12 = 42.

title: Deductive Syllogisms & Logic
description: Formal deductive logic & statement argument validation.

questions.questionText: Statement: All cats are animals. All animals have four legs. Conclusion: All cats have four legs.
questions.explanation: Since cats are animals, and all animals have four legs, then cats must have four legs according to the premises.

questions.questionText: Statement: Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are human. Conclusion: Some doctors are human.
questions.explanation: Since some doctors are teachers and all teachers are human, those doctors who are teachers are also human.

questions.questionText: Statement: No rectangles are circles. All squares are rectangles. Conclusion: No squares are circles.
questions.explanation: Since squares are subset of rectangles and rectangles have no intersection with circles, squares have no intersection with circles.

questions.questionText: Worker A can complete a task in 10 hours, and Worker B can complete the same task in 15 hours. If they work together, how many hours will it take to complete the task?
questions.explanation: The combined rate is: (1 / 10) + (1 / 15) = (3 / 30) + (2 / 30) = 5 / 30 = 1 / 6. Working together, they complete 1/6 of the task per hour, requiring 6 hours total.

questions.questionText: Train A leaves a station traveling east at 60 km/h. At the same time, Train B leaves traveling west at 90 km/h. How far apart will they be after 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Because they travel in opposite directions, their relative speed of separation is the sum: 60 + 90 = 150 km/h. In 2 hours, the total distance separated is 150 * 2 = 300 km.

questions.questionText: A car can travel 15 km on 1 liter of fuel. If a trip is 120 km long and fuel costs $2 per liter, how much will the fuel cost for a round trip?
questions.explanation: A round trip is 120 * 2 = 240 km. The fuel required is 240 / 15 = 16 liters. Total cost = 16 * $2 = $32.

questions.questionText: Task A depends on Task B, which depends on Task C. If Task C takes 3 hours, Task B takes 4 hours, and Task A takes 2 hours, and they must run sequentially, what is the total execution time?
questions.explanation: Because of the linear dependency (C -> B -> A), they cannot run in parallel. The total time is the sum of all tasks: 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 hours.

questions.questionText: A car traveling at 80 km/h is 40 km behind a truck traveling at 60 km/h in the same direction. How many hours will it take for the car to overtake the truck?
questions.explanation: The relative speed at which the car closes the gap is 80 - 60 = 20 km/h. To cover the 40 km gap, it will take: 40 / 20 = 2 hours.

questions.questionText: Pipe A can fill a water tank in 4 hours, while Pipe B can empty the same tank in 6 hours. If both pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: The net rate of filling per hour is: (1 / 4) - (1 / 6) = (3 / 12) - (2 / 12) = 1 / 12. Therefore, it will take 12 hours to completely fill the tank.

questions.questionText: A team of 5 workers can build a wall in 10 days. If 2 workers fall ill before the project starts, how many days will the remaining 3 workers take to complete the wall?
questions.explanation: Total work is measured in man-days: 5 workers * 10 days = 50 man-days. With 3 workers, the duration is: 50 / 3 = 16.67 days.

questions.questionText: At 80 km/h, a car consumes 1 liter of fuel per 16 km. At 120 km/h, consumption increases to 1 liter per 12 km. How much more fuel (in liters) is consumed at 120 km/h compared to 80 km/h for a 240 km journey?
questions.explanation: At 80 km/h, fuel used = 240 / 16 = 15 liters. At 120 km/h, fuel used = 240 / 12 = 20 liters. The excess fuel is: 20 - 15 = 5 liters.

questions.questionText: An engine assembly takes 4 hours (Path 1), and a chassis assembly takes 6 hours (Path 2). Both must be finished before the final assembly (2 hours) can begin. If Paths 1 and 2 run in parallel, what is the total production time?
questions.explanation: Since Path 1 and Path 2 run in parallel, the stage takes max(4, 6) = 6 hours. Adding the final 2-hour assembly stage gives: 6 + 2 = 8 hours.

questions.questionText: A train 200 meters long is traveling at a speed of 36 km/h. How many seconds will it take to completely cross a bridge that is 300 meters long?
questions.explanation: First convert speed: 36 km/h * (5/18) = 10 m/s. The total distance to cross is the train length + bridge length = 200 + 300 = 500 meters. Time = 500 / 10 = 50 seconds.
